type.name: Anatomy 3D
type.description: A real 3D model you can rotate and zoom. A structure lights up and you type or pick its name, or you tap the structure the prompt describes, or you drag names onto numbered pins. After answering, tap any structure to see what it is. Scenes ship as type assets (scene-<id>.bin), shared by every card.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Shown above the model (also the card's title in lists).

fields.name: region
fields.description: Small label over the prompt, e.g. 'Left arm · anterior'. Never the answer.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: name: type the glowing structure. choose: pick its name from options. locate: tap the structure the prompt describes. label: drag names onto pins.

fields.name: scene
fields.description: Scene id; the card loads the asset scene-<id>.bin.

fields.name: target
fields.description: Part keys of the answer (name/choose: they glow; locate: any of them counts).

fields.name: answer
fields.description: The answer's name. build.py fills it with the target part's label.

fields.name: accept
fields.description: name: other accepted names (Latin, Portuguese, synonyms).

fields.name: choices
fields.description: choose: wrong options shown next to the answer.

fields.name: pins
fields.description: label: part keys that get numbered pins.

fields.name: anchors
fields.description: label: one [x, y, z] (mm) per pin, computed by build.py.

fields.name: distractors
fields.description: label: extra names in the bank that belong to no pin.

fields.name: hide
fields.description: Part keys not drawn for this card.

fields.name: view
fields.description: Camera override { az, el, zoom } (degrees; az 0 = anterior, 90 = patient's left).

fields.name: xray
fields.description: Start with every other structure see-through (name, choose, label).

fields.name: keys
fields.description: Every part key of the scene, in asset order. Written by build.py.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: Every part's name, in asset order. Written by build.py; shown when exploring after answering.

items.deck: Human anatomy::1 Bones::Pelvis and lower limb

fields.note: The **femur** is the longest and strongest bone. Proximally: head, neck (angle of about 125° with the shaft), greater and lesser trochanters joined by the intertrochanteric line in front and crest behind. Distally: medial and lateral condyles and epicondyles, with the patellar surface in front. The linea aspera on the back of the shaft anchors the adductors, vastus medialis and vastus lateralis.

fields.prompt: Tap the chamber that forms most of the base (posterior surface) of the heart.
fields.note: The **left atrium** forms most of the base of the heart and receives the four pulmonary veins. It lies directly in front of the oesophagus, so an enlarged left atrium (mitral stenosis) can indent a barium swallow and cause dysphagia. Transoesophageal echo uses this closeness.

fields.prompt: Drag each name onto its pin.
fields.note: Left lateral view of the skull. **Frontal** in front, **parietal** on the roof, **occipital** behind, **temporal** low on the side above the ear, and the **zygomatic** at the cheek. The ethmoid barely shows on the outside of the skull; look for it in the medial orbital wall.

fields.prompt: Tap the gyrus that contains Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere.
fields.note: Broca's area = pars opercularis and triangularis of the **inferior frontal gyrus** (Brodmann 44, 45). A lesion gives non-fluent (expressive) aphasia: effortful, telegraphic speech with relatively preserved comprehension, often with right face and arm weakness because the motor cortex lies next to it.

The **pulmonary trunk** leaves the right ventricle (conus arteriosus), runs up and to the left in front of the ascending aorta, and divides under the aortic arch into the right and left pulmonary arteries. The ligamentum arteriosum joins the start of the left pulmonary artery to the arch.
